examples.label: Grep the whole filesystem for the flag format
Find files containing 'flag' under the cwd

notes: Fast way to grab a lab flag or spot leaked secrets once you have any elevated read. Redirect stderr to /dev/null so permission-denied noise doesn't bury the hit.

recommended.note: Broaden to configs/keys/secrets, not just flags.

name: Enumeration - Flag / Keyword Search
description: Recursively hunt for flags or a keyword across the filesystem or a specific directory - handy on exam/lab boxes once you have read access.

defense.why_it_works: After gaining elevated access, sensitive files (flags, credentials, private keys) may be stored anywhere on the filesystem. find / with -name and -type traverses the entire filesystem including directories inaccessible before privilege escalation, locating files by name pattern that were previously hidden.
defense.prerequisites: Root or elevated access. Filesystem traversal capability.
defense.impact: Sensitive data discovery: flags, private keys, credentials, database dumps, backup files -- all discoverable once root access is obtained.
defense.detection: Auditd: find command traversing sensitive directories (/root, /etc, /var/backups). Unusual read access to /root/ by non-root account. SIEM: mass file open events from a single process.
defense.artifacts: Auditd: mass file stat/open syscalls across filesystem | Process audit log (find executed with / as root)
defense.prevention: Encrypt sensitive files at rest. Apply DAC (file permissions) and MAC (SELinux/AppArmor) to limit access even for root. Segregate secrets using secrets managers. Ensure flag/credential files are not placed in predictable locations.
defense.misconfiguration: Sensitive files (credentials, flags, backups) stored as world-readable or in directories accessible post-escalation with predictable names.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Insecure storage of sensitive data
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root /root/flag.txt
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root /var/backups/db_backup.sql
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict sensitive file access
chmod 600 /root/flag.txt
chmod 700 /root/
# Enable SELinux
setenforce 1
# Use encrypted storage for secrets (LUKS, Vault)
